title: Twist an Oreo open, one hand holding the top wafer while the other turns the base, and lay both halves on the plate
instruction: Open this Oreo into its two halves and put both halves on the plate.
context: Twisting an Oreo open is a near-universal habit (the brand's own 'twist, lick, dunk'). Physically it is torsional failure of the creme: the wafers must be counter-rotated about their shared axis (about 0.1 N m) and the creme lets go of one wafer (Owens et al., Phys. Fluids 2022). Pulling or prying a 3.5 mm wafer held only at its rim does not open it; one hand must hold one wafer still while the other turns the other.
setup: Units cm, kg; x forward from the arm bases, y left; table top 74.75 cm up. Task objects: Nabisco Oreo Original sandwich cookie lying flat on the table at (44, 0): two chocolate wafers 4.4 dia x 0.35 (top 0.0039; base 0.0039 with the creme), white creme disc 3.5 dia x 0.4 on the base wafer, 1.1 thick overall, 0.0113 in all. Plastic plate (SimReady), 17.2 x 17.7 x 2.6, 0.15, centred at (25, 0). Distractors, ignored by scoring (SimReady): 8 oz drinking glass 6.6 dia x 10, 0.40, at (52, 17); plastic spoon 15.7 x 3.5 x 1.1, 0.02, at (53, -15) yaw 1.2 rad; ceramic mug 11.4 x 9 x 8, 0.30, at (12, 25).
scoring: Opened = the two wafers were turned at least 10 degrees against each other and have separated (real trial: in the last video frame before the halves part, a tick drawn across both wafers' rims is offset at least 3.5 mm along the rim). Cracked = a fingertip pressed on a wafer with more than 15 N for 2 control steps in a row (real trial: the end photo shows a crack, chip or broken-off edge longer than 2 mm on either wafer). On the plate = resting on its floor: the plate upright (within 10 degrees), the half's centre within 64 mm of the plate's centre, and its lowest point 0 to 4 mm above the plate's floor surface (1 mm tolerance below). 0 if the cookie was never opened, a wafer cracked, or a half ever fell off the table (centre over 3 cm below the table top). 1.0: opened; both halves on the plate, each lying flat (within 20 degrees, either face up), centres at least 45 mm apart, every fingertip at least 3 cm from both halves, both halves still, all held 1 s. 0.75: opened and both halves on the plate with the fingertips 3 cm clear, without the rest of 1.0. 0.5: opened, otherwise (a half still held, or off the plate).
reset_notes: Each trial consumes one cookie: use a fresh Oreo from the same pack, laid flat on its tape mark with the base wafer (the one the creme stays on in a test twist from that pack) down, with eight marker ticks across its rim every 45 degrees. Wipe the plate of crumbs.
fidelity: The wafers are rigid 16-sided discs at the cookie's size and mass (SimReady has no Oreo). The creme is a twist joint: a torsion spring that lets go for good past 10 degrees at 0.1 N m (Owens et al. 2022), rigid in pull and bending. Wafers cannot crack in the sim, so cracking is scored: a fingertip force over 15 N on a wafer (estimated from biscuit bend data) for 2 steps counts as cracked. Plate and distractors are SimReady props.
